title: Grade 3 Science — Wed, Jun 11
description: Plant Kingdom — Day 3 of 5: Stems — types and functions
subject: science

questions.question: The main job of the stem is to:
options: Support the plant and carry water from roots to leaves
questions.explanation: The stem holds the plant upright and transports water, minerals, and food between roots and leaves.

questions.question: A stem that is soft and green is called a ____ stem.
questions.explanation: Herbaceous stems are soft, green, and flexible. Examples: rose, sunflower seedling, and grass.

questions.question: A stem that is hard, thick, and brown is called a ____ stem.
questions.explanation: Woody stems are hard and strong. Trees like mango, neem, and oak have woody stems (called trunks).

questions.question: Which plant has an underground stem that we eat?
questions.explanation: Potato is a modified underground stem (tuber) that stores food. We eat the swollen underground stem.

questions.question: The stem of a cactus is:
options: Modified to store water in dry conditions
questions.explanation: The cactus has a thick, fleshy stem that stores water. Its leaves are modified into spines to reduce water loss.

questions.question: Water absorbed by the roots travels up to the leaves through tiny tubes in the:
questions.explanation: The stem has a network of tiny tubes (xylem vessels) that carry water and minerals from roots up to the leaves.

questions.question: Onion is actually a modified stem called a:
questions.explanation: An onion is a bulb — a modified underground stem with fleshy leaves that store food.

questions.question: Ginger is a modified stem that grows:
questions.explanation: Ginger is a rhizome — a horizontally growing underground stem. We use ginger as a spice in Indian cooking.

questions.question: What are the points on a stem where leaves and buds grow called?
questions.explanation: Nodes are the points on the stem where leaves, buds, and branches arise. Internodes are the spaces between nodes.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a climbing plant whose stem wraps around a support?
questions.explanation: Money plant is a climber — its stem winds around supports. Cucumber and bean are also climbers.

questions.question: The trunk of a tree is a type of:
questions.explanation: The trunk of a tree is a thick woody stem. It supports the heavy branches and carries water upward.

questions.question: Which of the following carries food made in the leaves DOWN to the rest of the plant?
questions.explanation: Phloem tubes in the stem carry food (sugar made in leaves) to all other parts of the plant.

questions.question: A creeper plant spreads along the ground because its stem:
options: Is too weak to stand, so it grows horizontally
questions.explanation: Creepers have weak stems that cannot stand upright. They spread along the ground. Examples: pumpkin, watermelon, strawberry.

questions.question: Sugarcane is used to make sugar because its stem stores:
questions.explanation: Sugarcane stems store large amounts of sucrose (table sugar), which is extracted by crushing the stems.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the stem?
options: Carrying water from roots to leaves
Carrying food from leaves to roots
questions.explanation: Absorbing water from soil is done by roots, not the stem. The stem only transports what the roots absorb.
